cards.text: Paul is writing to the believers in Ephesus, and he's just told the Gentiles among them they're not strangers anymore but members of God's household. Now he starts a new thought, and he opens it by describing himself.

cards.question: Paul starts his new thought by describing himself. What does he call himself?

cards.text: Paul says he's a prisoner for the sake of the Gentiles, and then his sentence just stops mid-thought. Friend, I respect it, because I once started a story for the dead batteries in my old junk drawer and finished it a WEEK later.
So Paul heads down a side road. He says they've surely heard about the stewardship of God's grace that was given to him.

cards.question: Paul says the stewardship of God's grace was given to him for someone. Who?

cards.text: And what's this stewardship about? Paul calls it a mystery, and he didn't dream it up on his own.

cards.question: Paul says the mystery was made known to him by ___.
Paul says this letter is the first time he's ever written to them about the mystery.

cards.text: Paul says that when they read what he wrote, they'll understand his insight into the mystery of Christ. And here's the WILD part: people in other generations never had it made known to them the way it's being revealed now.

cards.question: Paul says the Spirit has now revealed the mystery of Christ. To whom?

cards.text: So what's this mystery that stayed under wraps for generation after generation? Paul finally spells it out, and it's about the Gentiles.

cards.question: Through the gospel, what does Paul say is true of the Gentiles?

answers.text: They are fellow heirs in Christ Jesus
They are guests at Israel's table
They are servants to God's people

cards.question: Paul says the Gentiles get a smaller share of the promise in Christ Jesus than everyone else.

cards.text: Fellow heirs. Fellow members of the body. Fellow partakers of the promise. That's THREE fellows in one verse, friend, and nobody's left standing outside the door!
Now Paul talks about his own part in all this. He became a servant of this gospel.

cards.question: How does Paul say he became a servant of the gospel?

answers.text: By the gift of God's grace
By his training as a Pharisee
By a vote of the apostles

cards.question: Paul calls himself the greatest of all the saints.

cards.text: Paul calls himself less than the LEAST of all the saints. Friend, I lived at the very bottom of a junk drawer for years, and even I never found a spot that low.

cards.question: Paul says grace was given to him for a job. What is he to preach to the Gentiles?

cards.text: And it's not only for the Gentiles. Paul's also supposed to shine a light for everyone on the stewardship of this mystery.

cards.question: Paul says this mystery was kept hidden for ages past. Where was it kept?

answers.text: In God who created all things
In the scrolls of the prophets

cards.text: Now Paul zooms WAY out. God had a purpose in all this, and the audience is bigger than you'd ever guess.

cards.question: Through the church, who does Paul say should now be shown the manifold wisdom of God?

answers.text: The rulers and authorities in the heavenly realms
The kings and governors of the Roman Empire
The elders and priests of the people of Israel

cards.text: Through the CHURCH, friend! Regular folks putting God's wisdom on display, and Paul says it lines up with a purpose God accomplished in Christ Jesus our Lord.

cards.question: Paul calls this purpose a brand new plan God came up with recently.

cards.text: So what does that mean for the people reading this letter? Paul says that in Christ, and through faith in Him, we may enter God's presence.

cards.question: Paul says that in Christ we may enter God's presence with boldness and ___.

cards.text: Boldness and CONFIDENCE! Not peeking out all nervous, the way I used to every single time that drawer slid open.
Then Paul brings up his sufferings for them, and he has a request.

cards.question: Paul asks them not to be ___ because of his sufferings for them.
Paul says his sufferings for them are their glory.

findings.problem: The opening card states a fact from the previous passage: Paul has just told the Gentiles they're no longer strangers but members of God's household (Ephesians 2:19). The card gives no reference for it and cites only Ephesians 3:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The joke makes up a new event in the drawer: Papa Dorin starting a story for the dead batteries and finishing it a week later. The backstory doesn't include this, and the allowance for made-up moments covers only his bakery, not the drawer.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'The Gentiles he's writing to,' depends on Ephesians 3:1 ('for the sake of you Gentiles') to say who 'you' is in 3:2. The card cites only Ephesians 3:2.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower. A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: The setup line 'he didn't dream it up on his own' rules out the wrong answer 'study' on the next card, a fill in the blank for 'made known to him by ___'.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The text doesn't say what 'as I have already written briefly' (3:3) refers to. Verse 4, 'In reading this,' points to earlier in this same letter. If that is the reference, then this letter is the first time he's written to them about the mystery, and the statement is true. Marking it False settles a question the text leaves open, and a baker could argue for True.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The line 'nobody's left standing outside the door' goes beyond Ephesians 3:6, which says the Gentiles are fellow heirs through the gospel. It doesn't say nobody is left out. As written, the line can be read as a claim about Scripture, not a joke.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank asks the baker to supply the exact word of the line, 'not to be ___ because of my sufferings.' The setup ('he has a request') gives no meaning to reason from, and discouraged, ashamed and surprised are all believable. Getting it right comes down to guessing the wording.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
